bear: Cash flow is negative and capital spending is set to rise significantly next year.
Search and ad growth slowed noticeably, and the quarter missed on sales and earnings.
Alphabet sold new shares and took on debt, which dilutes owners and adds risk.
Buybacks stopped, so a key source of per-share support is gone.

bull.text: Cloud revenue more than doubled and its operating profit more than tripled to $11.1B.

bull: Cloud backlog of $561B gives unusual visibility into future revenue.
Overall operating profit grew faster than sales, showing the business still scales well.
Analysts mostly rate it Buy, with an average target far above the current price.

items.title: 2027 spending plan and Q4 results
items.detail: Management will give 2027 capital spending details. Some outlets expect it above $300B.

items.title: TPU chip system sales ramp
items.detail: Alphabet sells its own AI chips to customers. A meaningful revenue ramp is expected in 2027.

items.title: Backlog turning into revenue
items.detail: About $308B of Cloud backlog is expected to convert within 24 months.

items.title: Search growth stabilizing
items.detail: Search queries are at a five-year high, yet ad revenue growth slowed.

items.title: Spending outruns cash earned
items.detail: Capital spending of $51.4B beat operating cash flow of $42.3B. If Cloud demand cools, Alphabet is left with expensive, underused equipment.

items.title: Expectations still high
items.detail: Even after the drop, the stock prices in strong growth. Cloud cannot double forever, so a slowdown would hurt.

items.title: Core ad business slowing
items.detail: Services growth fell from 15% to 11% in one quarter. Rivals such as Microsoft ($MSFT) are also competing hard in AI.

items.title: Earnings are noisy
items.detail: Large swings in investment values, such as an SpaceX stake markdown, make profit hard to read.

verdict.oneLiner: Alphabet's AI business is booming, but it is spending more cash than it earns, and the stock just fell about 10%.

bottomLine.holding: Holding looks reasonable, since Cloud growth and profits are real. Watch whether free cash flow turns positive and whether the 2027 spending number is far above expectations.
bottomLine.considering: The business is strong, and the lower price helps. Starting small makes sense only if you accept years of heavy spending before cash returns.

threeThings.risk: Alphabet is spending more on AI data centers than it earns in cash, and says next year's spending will jump.
threeThings.watch: Alphabet will give its 2027 spending plan in February, and investors want proof that Cloud's order backlog turns into cash.
threeThings.growth: Revenue grew 25% to $127.6B last quarter, helped by Cloud doubling, though the core Search and ads business slowed.

headline: Cloud Doubles, But Cash Burn Rattles Alphabet Investors
